text.p: Shareholders of Venezuelan paints and packaging company Corimon will consider a 33 billion bolivar ($70 million) share issue on December 2 as part of a continued move to restructure the company's debt, the company said Wednesday.
Corimon said the share issue would involve 3.3 billion preferential Class B shares made available to creditors at a nominal value of 10 bolivars each.
It would be the second such share issue in recent months following another 3.3 billion share issue of Class B shares in late July.
Corimon shares resumed trade on the Caracas Stock Exchange in late October after an eight-month suspension following disappointing financial results.
Corimon reported a third quarter net profit of 700 million bolivars, down from 1.782 billion bolivars in the same period in 1995.
